done_when: The owner switches a repo to agent merges with one command run in their own terminal

findings.body: The replacement matches only an unquoted `merge` at column one. A valid `forge.toml` with `  merge = "human"` or `"merge" = "human"` passes config validation, but this code inserts a second top-level key. Forge then commits invalid TOML, and `forge close` cannot finish the switch. [TOML 1.0.0](https://toml.io/en/v1.0.0) permits both key forms and forbids duplicate keys.
findings.title: Handle valid indented or quoted merge keys

findings.body: This collision check looks only for a local branch. If `origin/fix/let-the-agent-merge` belongs to another fix but has no local branch or worktree, the command creates and commits a new local fix under that name before its push fails as non-fast-forward. Rerunning repeats the failed push rather than refusing the collision without changes. The existing `fix start` path checks remote refs too (`src/forge/task.py:223-228`).
findings.title: Check for an existing remote switch branch before creating a worktree

findings.body: `forge fix start "Enable" --done ...` can create the valid item `fix/enable` through the existing slug logic (`src/forge/task.py:217-232`). Its `forge merge enable` invocation now always enters the switch command. From an agent shell it refuses as owner-only; once agent merges are on it refuses as already enabled. Forge can no longer merge that ready fix.
findings.title: Preserve merging an existing fix named enable

findings.body: A differently named fix that changes `merge` can reach Ready in an unsigned prototype. `forge close` correctly says a human merges it (`src/forge/close.py:142`), but this condition uses the prototype's effective agent setting (`src/forge/repo.py:174-177`) and prints `Next: forge merge <item>`. That command then refuses the setting change at `src/forge/merge.py:59-60`. Detect the setting change here so `forge next` gives the owner a usable step.
findings.title: Keep forge next on the owner path for other merge-setting fixes

findings.body: `_enable` requires both `why` and `done_when` to recognize its fix (`src/forge/merge.py:174`), but `forge next` checks only `why`. A normal `forge fix start` with that same why and a different done-when is treated as the switch: at Started, `forge next` tells the owner to run `forge merge enable`, which creates or resumes a different fix and does nothing for this one.
findings.title: Identify the switch fix by its full recorded contract in forge next

why: Nothing in the flow can switch a repo to agent merges: Forge tells the owner to ask the agent, and the agent's own permission checks rightly refuse to loosen a gate on itself
